affected_system: air-quality surveillance, exposure reduction, and respiratory-health response
alternatives: activate a bounded reserve from forecast risk bands for daily pollution alert and respiratory service demand
use rolling forecasts and conservative capacity triggers for daily pollution alert and respiratory service demand
pair weather-source and lag-conditioned joint forecasting with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Monitor data retain calibration, siting, uptime, and spatial-representativeness metadata.
Exposure, diagnosis, care use, and service complaints are not interchangeable outcomes.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue ordinary capacity planning for daily pollution alert and respiratory service demand.

constraints.description: The air-quality exposure and respiratory health forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: environmental health director and air-quality program lead
decision_question: What pollutant and respiratory-service workload envelope should public-health operations prepare for?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The air-quality exposure and respiratory health forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
independence_key.decision_object: daily pollution alert and respiratory service demand
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for daily pollution alert and respiratory service demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.
independence_key.primary_outcome: respiratory response demand above available capacity

intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting daily pollution alert and respiratory service demand, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: respiratory response demand above available capacity
distributional gap in respiratory response demand above available capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call forecast service demand diagnosed disease or pollutant-attributable illness.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for daily pollution alert and respiratory service demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

title: Forecast air-quality alerts and respiratory service demand
transportability_risks: Pollutant mixtures, indoor infiltration, source profiles, coding, and monitor coverage differ.
Modeled concentration may not represent personal exposure.
